My reasoning:

I been farming this land 40 years, so I know what works. I do the same as last year — why change? My neighbors all plant wheat in October, maize in June, and we all do about the same.

For wheat on my 12 mu, I put down 2 bags of compound fertilizer per mu before planting — that's 100 jin, no, 100 kg per mu. That's what the dealer in town sells, 15-15-15 he calls it. Then when the wheat wakes up in spring and starts to joint, I spread urea, maybe 20 kg per mu. My neighbor Old Wang, his wheat looked yellow last year so he added more, got 550 kg. I don't want yellow wheat, so I put enough. Better waste a little fertilizer than lose the harvest — a bad harvest is a disaster, extra fertilizer is just some money.

I water the wheat before winter once, then green-up water, then at jointing, then at grain filling. Four times. I have the well right there. I spray for weeds once in spring, then for aphids when I see them, maybe once more for the yellow leaves disease. My wheat usually gives 500 kg per mu, sometimes 520.

For maize, I plant right after wheat comes off, no plowing — just seed straight into the stubble with the machine. Everyone does it this way now. I use the hybrid seed, Zhengdan or whatever the dealer has good this year. Two bags compound fertilizer per mu at planting with the seeder, then urea 20 kg per mu when it's knee-high. Summer rain waters it usually, but if July is dry I pump once from the well. Spray once for borers. Maize gives me about 550 kg per mu.

I buy hybrid maize seed because everyone does — the old seeds don't yield. For wheat I use improved seed from the station, bag I bought last year I saved some.

decision.reasoning_summary: I farm the same way as last year and the same as my neighbors — 40 years doing this, I know what my land needs. Two bags of compound fertilizer per mu at planting for both crops, then urea topdressing when the plants need it. Better to use enough fertilizer than risk a yellow crop — wasting some money is nothing compared to losing yield. Wheat gets four waterings from my well; maize mostly drinks the summer rain, I pump once if July is dry. Rotary till before wheat, direct seed maize into the stubble like everyone does now. Hybrid maize seed and improved wheat seed from the dealer — the old seeds don't give yield anymore.
